Content: Given the information in the graph, in which of the following states would an individual's vote likely have more influence?

A.Choice: Wyoming

Key.Rationale: The graph shows that individuals casting votes in Wyoming would have more influence because of the smaller number of residents `text(per electoral vote)`.

B.Choice: West Virginia

Key.Rationale: The graph shows that individuals casting votes in West Virginia would not have as much influence as those in other states because of the larger number of residents `text(per vote)`.

C.Choice: Alabama

Key.Rationale: The graph shows that individuals casting votes in Alabama would not have as much influence as those in other states because of the larger number of residents `text(per vote)`.

D.Choice: California

Key.Rationale: The graph shows that individuals casting votes in California would not have as much influence as those in other states because of the larger number of residents `text(per vote)`.

Content: The data in the graph best illustrate which of the following common criticisms of the electoral college?

A.Choice: Small states have fewer electoral votes than large states and therefore have no impact on presidential elections.

Key.Rationale: The chart does not illustrate the criticism that smaller states have fewer electoral votes and so do not have an impact on presidential elections.

B.Choice: Individuals in small-population states have a greater impact on the electoral college than individuals in large-population states.

Key.Rationale: The chart best illustrates the criticism that citizens living in states with smaller populations have a larger impact in the electoral college.

C.Choice: Candidates from states with a large number of electoral votes have a major advantage in the electoral college.

Key.Rationale: The chart does not illustrate the criticism that candidates from states with a large number of electoral votes have an advantage in the electoral college.

D.Choice: Smaller states have more electoral votes than larger states, which distorts the popular vote.

Key.Rationale: The chart does not illustrate the criticism that smaller states have more electoral college votes than larger states.

Content: According to the bar graph, which of the following statements will be true in the `text(year 2060)`?

A.Choice: The `text(percentage)` of those identifying as Asian alone will be less than it was in `text(2012)`.

Key.Rationale: The graph shows the `text(percentage)` of people identifying as Asian increasing.

B.Choice: Those identifying as White alone will remain a majority.

Key.Rationale: The graph shows the `text(percentage)` of people identifying as White alone remaining a majority at `69%`.

C.Choice: Those identifying as Hispanic White will be `31%` of the population.

Key.Rationale: The graph does not show the `text(percentage)` of people identifying as Hispanic White.

D.Choice: The `text(percentage)` of those identifying as Black alone will be less than it was in `text(2012)`.

Key.Rationale: The graph shows the `text(percentage)` of the population identifying as Black alone increasing from `13%` to `15%`.

Content: Which of the following is a likely effect of the trend depicted in the bar graph on voting and elections?

A.Choice: There will be fewer restrictions placed on voting.

Key.Rationale: Demographic trends do not necessarily affect restrictions on voting.

B.Choice: Voter turnout is likely to increase among non-Whites.

Key.Rationale: The demographic shift depicted in the graph does not necessarily result in any specific change in voter turnout.

C.Choice: The Democratic Party will win more elections, based on current voting trends.

Key.Rationale: The demographic shift will benefit the Democratic Party if current voting trends continue.

D.Choice: There will be more retrospective voting among young voters.

Key.Rationale: Demographic changes do not necessarily have an effect on retrospective voting.

Content: Which of the following statements is most accurately supported by the data in the table?

A.Choice: President Clinton greatly reduced the use of presidential signing statements compared with his predecessors.

Key.Rationale: President Clinton issued more signing statements than both of his predecessors.

B.Choice: While President George W. Bush issued fewer signing statements than President Clinton, his included more objections than President Clinton's.

Key.Rationale: George W. Bush did issue fewer signing statements, but his included `127` objections, as opposed to Clinton's `70`.

C.Choice: President Clinton's brief access to the power of the line-item veto allowed him to issue fewer signing statements that raised concerns about legislation.

Key.Rationale: The table shows that President Clinton issued the most signing statements of those listed, which would not support the theory that temporary access to the line-item veto allowed him to issue fewer signing statements.

D.Choice: President George W. Bush was forced to issue more signing statements as a direct result of the terrorist attacks of `text(September 11, 2001)`.

Key.Rationale: The terrorist attacks of `text(September 11, 2001)`, did not necessitate more signing statements; George W. Bush actually issued fewer signing statements.

Content: Which of the following represents a reason that a president might use a signing statement to express displeasure with a bill as opposed to issuing a veto?

A.Choice: The president may have objections to provisions of a bill but does not want to risk Congress overriding a veto.

Key.Rationale: The president can use a signing statement to register protest when a veto override is likely.

B.Choice: Congress has severely curtailed the power of the president to withhold funds for bills that have been adopted.

Key.Rationale: The president does not have control over the national budget and cannot control approval of funding levels.

C.Choice: The Supreme Court is hesitant to acknowledge the president's power to veto legislation.

Key.Rationale: The president's power to veto is enumerated in the Constitution.

D.Choice: The president wants to ensure executive agencies do not spend the money appropriated by Congress.

Key.Rationale: Signing statements do not allow the president to prevent agencies from spending money appropriated by Congress.

Content: Which of the following statements presents the most important limitation of the data in the graph?

A.Choice: The time frame for the data is misleading.

Key.Rationale: The time frame for the data is not misleading.

B.Choice: There is no information about the total number of state legislators.

Key.Rationale: `text(One)` important limitation of the chart is that it does not tell the total number of all state legislators. This information is relevant for understanding the cause of the trend.

C.Choice: There are insufficient data points to detect a trend.

Key.Rationale: There are enough data points to detect a clear trend.

D.Choice: The trend over time is potentially misleading and would be easier to read in a pie chart.

Key.Rationale: These data do not need a pie chart to be clearly depicted.

Content: Which of the following is most likely responsible for the increase in the number of southern African American state legislators between `text(1960)` and `text(1992)` as shown in the graph?

A.Choice: The Civil Rights Act of `text(1964)`

Key.Rationale: The Civil Rights Act of `text(1964)` did not extend any new protections to African Americans in the voting booth.

B.Choice: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka (`text(1954)`)

Key.Rationale: In Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka (`text(1954)`), the Supreme Court did not extend any new protections to African Americans in the voting booth.

C.Choice: The Voting Rights Act of `text(1965)`

Key.Rationale: The Voting Rights Act of `text(1965)` made it illegal to discriminate against African Americans in polling places in the South which is a likely explanation for the increase in African American legislators.

D.Choice: The `text(Nineteenth)` Amendment

Key.Rationale: The `text(Nineteenth)` Amendment did not extend any additional protections to African Americans in the voting booth.

Content: Which of the following statements reflects a pattern in the line graph?

A.Choice: Nixon had the highest approval ratings of any president in the graph.

Key.Rationale: The graph does not show that Nixon had the highest approval ratings of any president represented.

B.Choice: Most presidents exit office with lower approval ratings than when they entered office.

Key.Rationale: The graph shows that most presidents exit office with lower approval ratings than they had when they were elected.

C.Choice: Most presidents begin their term with approval ratings lower than `50%`.

Key.Rationale: The graph does not show that most presidents begin their terms with approval ratings lower than `50%`.

D.Choice: Eisenhower had the lowest approval ratings of any president in the graph.

Key.Rationale: The graph does not show that Eisenhower had the lowest approval ratings of any president represented.

Content: Which of the following correctly identifies an implication of the line graph?

A.Choice: Presidents are far more likely to make changes to the bureaucracy at the end of a `text(second)` term than at the beginning of a `text(first)` term.

Key.Rationale: Presidents are not more likely to make changes to the bureaucracy at the end of the `text(second)` term than at the beginning of a `text(first)` term.

B.Choice: Congress is more likely to act on a president's policy proposal at the beginning of a `text(first)` term than at the end of a `text(second)` term.

Key.Rationale: The most accurate implication is that Congress is more likely to act on a president's policy at the beginning of a `text(first)` term than at the end of `text(second)` term.

C.Choice: The Supreme Court is more likely to rule on an important case at the beginning of a `text(first)` term than at the end of a `text(second)` term.

Key.Rationale: The Supreme Court is not more likely to rule on an important case at the beginning of a `text(first)` term than at the end of a `text(second)` term.

D.Choice: Presidents are more likely to send troops into conflict at the end of a `text(second)` term than at the beginning of a `text(first)` term.

Key.Rationale: Presidents are not more likely to send troops into conflict at the end of the `text(second)` term than at the beginning of a `text(first)` term.

Content: Which of the following newspaper headlines best summarizes the excerpt from Washington's Farewell Address?

A.Choice: Washington Boasts of the Potential of the New Republic

Key.Rationale: “Washington Boasts of the Potential of the New Republic” does not summarize Washington's Farewell Address.

B.Choice: Washington Warns of Dangerous Party Factions

Key.Rationale: “Washington Warns of Dangerous Party Factions” is the newspaper headline that best summarizes Washington's Farewell Address.

C.Choice: Washington Endorses a Stronger Executive Branch

Key.Rationale: “Washington Endorses a Stronger Executive Branch” does not summarize Washington's Farewell Address.

D.Choice: Washington Takes Negative View of Checks and Balances

Key.Rationale: “Washington Takes Negative View of Checks and Balances” does not summarize Washington's Farewell Address.

Content: In what respect does the Constitution address Washington's concern regarding the “spirit of encroachment” expressed in the excerpt?

A.Choice: The Constitution distributes power across national institutions.

Key.Rationale: Distributing power across national institutions was designed to address the “spirit of encroachment” mentioned in the passage.

B.Choice: The Constitution provides for equal representation of all citizens in Congress.

Key.Rationale: Some features of the Constitution provide for equal representation for citizens in Congress, but this does not address Washington's concern in the passage.

C.Choice: The Constitution requires a simple majority vote in Congress to overturn a veto.

Key.Rationale: The Constitution does not require a simple majority to override a veto.

D.Choice: The Constitution requires the Supreme Court to approve all legislation.

Key.Rationale: The Constitution does not require the Supreme Court to approve all legislation.

Content: Which of the following scenarios illustrates Washington's concerns?

A.Choice: An increasing number of voters are not turning out to vote in elections.

Key.Rationale: Washington does not express concern about voter turnout rates.

B.Choice: Federalism can lead to different public policy outcomes between states.

Key.Rationale: Washington does not express concern about different public policy outcomes in different states.

C.Choice: Ideological divisions within Congress can lead to partisan gridlock.

Key.Rationale: Washington expresses concern about parties interfering with the operation of good government. Gridlock is caused by parties not willing to work with each other to pass important legislation.

D.Choice: Members of the press fail to report on the illegal activities of certain members of the bureaucracy.

Key.Rationale: Washington does not express concern about members of the press not reporting on the illegal activities of the bureaucracy.

Content: By using the phrase “creative federalism,” President Johnson is most likely referring to which of the following features of the American system?

A.Choice: The relationship between the federal and state governments evolves over time and is flexible enough to permit new forms of interaction.

Key.Rationale: Johnson is referring to the evolving relationship between levels of government

B.Choice: National policymaking is constrained by the sharing of power between the `text(three)` branches of government.

Key.Rationale: Johnson is not referring to the constraints of power sharing.

C.Choice: The balance of power between the states and federal government has been trending toward more federal regulation and less state control.

Key.Rationale: Johnson is not referring to the trend toward more federal control over states.

D.Choice: Congress may use the commerce clause to address problems in public schools such as lack of resources and school safety.

Key.Rationale: Johnson is not referring to the commerce clause.

Content: Which of the following actions did President Johnson suggest he would take to address problems in public schools?

A.Choice: Driving down the cost of education by removing ineffective teachers

Key.Rationale: Johnson does not suggest removing ineffective teachers.

B.Choice: Calling on experts to advise the federal government in finding ways to improve public education

Key.Rationale: Johnson does suggest calling on experts to advise the federal government.

C.Choice: Increasing school accountability by requiring schools to show evidence of improvement

Key.Rationale: Johnson does not suggest increasing accountability for schools.

D.Choice: Scaling back the role of the federal government and allowing state and local governments to take the lead in education policy

Key.Rationale: Johnson does not suggest scaling back the federal government role in education.

Content: Which of the following explains President Johnson's motivation for the speech in relation to his role as the head of the executive branch?

A.Choice: President Johnson believes that Congress will soon pass a bill on education reform, and he would like to be able to claim credit for it.

Key.Rationale: Johnson is not attempting to anticipate what legislation Congress will pass, but rather influence what legislation Congress will pass.

B.Choice: President Johnson is seeking to use the bully pulpit as a means of promoting his agenda on public education.

Key.Rationale: Johnson is using the bully pulpit to promote an agenda.

C.Choice: President Johnson is expecting the Supreme Court to soon rule on the constitutionality of a law passed by the previous administration.

Key.Rationale: Johnson is not expecting the Supreme Court to rule on a law.

D.Choice: President Johnson is issuing an executive order calling on local governments to increase training for teachers and address poverty among students.

Key.Rationale: Johnson is not issuing an executive order.

Content: A liberal response to the “strained resources” of local government most likely would include

A.Choice: a reduction of federal income taxes so that state and local governments can use those resources

Key.Rationale: Liberals do not favor tax cuts as a means of helping local governments.

B.Choice: less federal regulation and more authority for local school boards to create curricula and standards

Key.Rationale: Liberals do not believe that less federal regulation and more authority for school boards will provide greater resources to local governments.

C.Choice: an increase in federal spending on public education and more programs aimed at helping lower-income communities

Key.Rationale: Liberals believe that an increase in federal spending on public education and more programs aimed at helping lower-income communities will provide greater resources to local governments.

D.Choice: encouraging state and local governments to offer vouchers so that students can attend private or charter schools

Key.Rationale: Liberals do not believe that school vouchers will provide greater resources to local governments.

Content: Which of the following statements best describes the information in the map?

A.Choice: Most states in the Northeast and West do not allow capital punishment.

Key.Rationale: Most states in the West do allow capital punishment.

B.Choice: Most states in the South and West allow capital punishment.

Key.Rationale: Most states in the South and West allow capital punishment.

C.Choice: Capital punishment is not allowed in Oklahoma (OK) and New Mexico (NM).

Key.Rationale: Oklahoma allows capital punishment.

D.Choice: Only `text(three)` states do not allow capital punishment.

Key.Rationale: More than three states do not allow capital punishment.

Content: Which of the following constitutional principles best explains why there is variation among states on the use of capital punishment?

A.Choice: Separation of powers

Key.Rationale: Separation of powers does not explain variation among the states.

B.Choice: Judicial review

Key.Rationale: Judicial review does not explain variation among the states.

C.Choice: Checks and balances

Key.Rationale: Checks and balances does not explain variation among the states.

D.Choice: Federalism

Key.Rationale: Federalism allows states to develop their own policies, and so it explains variation among the states.

Content: Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation of the political cartoon?

A.Choice: State governments have used the `text(Tenth)` Amendment to override the federal government's mandates.

Key.Rationale: The cartoon does not suggest that the `text(Tenth)` Amendment has been used to override federal mandates.

B.Choice: State governments are unwilling to share their budgetary surpluses with other states.

Key.Rationale: The cartoon does not suggest that state governments are unwilling to share their budgetary surpluses with other states.

C.Choice: State governments prefer federal funding but do not want federal oversight over how the money is spent.

Key.Rationale: The cartoon suggests that states want federal money, depicted by the money bag offered by Uncle Sam, but do not want federal oversight, depicted by the gesture of rejection given by the “states' rights” advocate to the paper that says “federal authority” held by Uncle Sam.

D.Choice: The fiscal irresponsibility of state governments has led to increased federal regulation on their budgetary priorities.

Key.Rationale: The cartoon does not suggest that fiscal irresponsibility has led to increased federal regulation.

Content: Which of the following policies would the states most likely prefer according to the political cartoon?

A.Choice: Federal mandates

Key.Rationale: States do not want federal mandates, according to the cartoon, since they involve federal oversight.

B.Choice: Regulatory preemption

Key.Rationale: Regulatory preemption is not a form of regulations that states want, according to the cartoon, since it involves federal oversight.

C.Choice: Block grants

Key.Rationale: Block grants provide money to states without great oversight by the federal government, which appeals to states, according the cartoon.

D.Choice: Categorical grants

Key.Rationale: Since categorical grants provide money to states but come with very specific instructions on how it is spent, states do not want them, according to the cartoon.

Content: Which of the following is true according to the diagram?

A.Choice: The Senate minority leader is as powerful as the Senate majority whip.

Key.Rationale: The diagram shows that the Senate minority leader and the Senate majority whip are from `text(two)` different parties and have different levels of power.

B.Choice: The Speaker of the House, in coordination with the House majority leader, appoints the House minority leader.

Key.Rationale: The diagram shows the Speaker of the House is above the House minority leader, and they are from `text(two)` different parties.

C.Choice: Unlike the House of Representatives, the Senate does not recognize political parties.

Key.Rationale: The diagram does not illustrate that the Senate does not recognize political parties.

D.Choice: Both chambers make use of a system of majority and minority whips.

Key.Rationale: The diagram illustrates the system of majority and minority whips used in the House of Representatives and the Senate to generate support on legislation.

Content: Based on your knowledge and the diagram, which of the following is true regarding the leadership structure of Congress?

A.Choice: The role of the minority leader in both the House of Representatives and the Senate is to coordinate a strategy for the minority party.

Key.Rationale: The minority leader in each house of Congress coordinates strategy for the minority party.

B.Choice: The vice president is responsible for creating and setting the legislative agenda for the Senate.

Key.Rationale: The vice president is responsible for casting a tie-breaking vote in the Senate but not for creating the legislative agenda.

C.Choice: The Speaker of the House has very little power to control members of the majority party in the House of Representatives.

Key.Rationale: `text(One)` of the Speaker's jobs is to be the leader of the House's majority party, and therefore the Speaker has considerable power to control members of the majority party.

D.Choice: The majority leaders in both chambers work to ensure that a bipartisan agenda is passed in the Congress.

Key.Rationale: The majority leaders in both chambers control their own agendas but do not work to ensure that a bipartisan agenda is passed.

Content: In the `text(1780s)`, proponents of the new Constitution cited Shays' Rebellion as an example in support of which of the following criticisms of the national government under the Articles of Confederation?

A.Choice: The national government did not provide sufficient protection of individual rights.

Key.Rationale: Sufficient protection of individual rights was not `text(one)` of the main criticisms of the Articles of Confederation stemming from Shays' Rebellion.

B.Choice: The lack of a centralized judiciary made enforcement of national laws difficult.

Key.Rationale: Shays' Rebellion did not illustrate the criticism that there was a lack of a centralized judiciary.

C.Choice: States with larger populations were underrepresented in Congress.

Key.Rationale: Concern about large-state representation in Congress was addressed in the Great Compromise, but it was not a criticism originating with Shays' Rebellion.

D.Choice: There was a lack of a national military power to address security concerns.

Key.Rationale: The inability of the national government to respond militarily to Shays' Rebellion showed that the government was not very strong.

Content: The majority party in the Senate is concerned that the Supreme Court has made a number of ideologically dangerous and controversial rulings. Which of the following actions would the Senate take in their attempt to limit the Supreme Court's power?

A.Choice: Replace the chief justice of the Supreme Court with someone with whom they agree with ideologically

Key.Rationale: The Senate does not have the power to replace Supreme Court justices.

B.Choice: Pass legislation that would limit the impact of the Supreme Court's recent rulings

Key.Rationale: The Senate can check the power of the Supreme Court by passing legislation that limits the impact of the Court's ruling.

C.Choice: Ratify a constitutional amendment limiting the Supreme Court's power

Key.Rationale: The Senate does not ratify constitutional amendments.

D.Choice: Enforce term limits for justices on the Supreme Court

Key.Rationale: There are no term limits for Supreme Court justices.

Content: Which of the following describes an effect of the `text(Twenty-Fourth)` Amendment?

A.Choice: It assured equal access to places of public accommodation regardless of race.

Key.Rationale: The `text(Twenty-Fourth)` Amendment had no impact on access to places of public accommodation.

B.Choice: It increased the importance of the Speaker of the House of Representatives.

Key.Rationale: The `text(Twenty-Fourth)` Amendment had no impact on the importance of the Speaker of the House of Representatives.

C.Choice: It reduced barriers to political participation on the basis of gender.

Key.Rationale: Gender was not the focus of the `text(Twenty-Fourth)` Amendment.

D.Choice: It eliminated poll taxes.

Key.Rationale: The `text(Twenty-Fourth)` Amendment eliminated poll taxes.

Content: Which of the following enumerated powers would permit Congress to stimulate the economy by hiring unemployed citizens?

A.Choice: The power to create immigration policies

Key.Rationale: Creating immigration policies does not directly lead to hiring unemployed citizens.

B.Choice: The power to regulate interstate commerce

Key.Rationale: Congress's enumerated interstate commerce power regulates commerce with foreign nations, among states, and with Native Americans.

C.Choice: The power to pass a federal budget

Key.Rationale: When passing a federal budget, Congress allocates funds to various programs; these could include a program to stimulate the economy by hiring unemployed citizens.

D.Choice: The power of legislative oversight

Key.Rationale: Congressional oversight includes reviewing, monitoring, and supervising various federal agencies, but it does not directly lead to economic stimuli programs.

Content: Which of the following is likely to occur as a result of new legislation regarding automobile safety?

A.Choice: The Supreme Court will be asked to review the legislation `text(annually)`.

Key.Rationale: The Supreme Court does not review any type of legislation `text(annually)`.

B.Choice: States will be empowered to begin automobile manufacturing.

Key.Rationale: New legislation about automobile safety is very unlikely to ask states to manufacture automobiles.

C.Choice: The Department of Transportation will be given discretionary authority to create auto regulations.

Key.Rationale: The Department of Transportation is the organization that has the authority to create new safety regulations for cars.

D.Choice: Mandatory spending will be required in all future federal budgeting for the program.

Key.Rationale: Mandatory spending on automobile safety legislation is highly unlikely and not required in all future federal budgeting.

Content: Which of the following best describes an exit poll?

A.Choice: A poll that asks voters at randomly selected voting places whom they voted for so that election results can be predicted more quickly

Key.Rationale: Exit polls help predict election results by asking voters at randomly selected polling places whom they voted for.

B.Choice: A poll conducted by having a computer randomly select phone numbers from around the country

Key.Rationale: Having a computer randomly select phone numbers nationally is useful for polls with random samples but does not describe an exit poll.

C.Choice: An opinion poll that is used to intentionally sway people's opinions by using false or misleading information in the conversation

Key.Rationale: False or misleading information is not part of the design of exit polls.

D.Choice: A poll that randomly samples a population to capture public opinion at a given time

Key.Rationale: Exit polls focus on randomly sampling selected voting places, not just random samples of the population.

Content: The Supreme Court issued a ruling that was unpopular with a majority of Americans. The president and Congress might be able to lessen the impact of the decision by

A.Choice: reducing the pay of the justices to pressure them to reverse their decision

Key.Rationale: The Constitution states that Congress cannot reduce the salaries of justices.

B.Choice: overruling the Supreme Court's decision by a `text(two-thirds)` vote in Congress

Key.Rationale: According to the Constitution, Congress cannot override a Supreme Court decision.

C.Choice: impeaching the justices in the majority

Key.Rationale: Congress does have the right to impeach a Supreme Court justice, but there must be good cause to do this. Impeaching the justices in the majority is not a step that Congress would take to lessen the impact of a decision.

D.Choice: refusing to actively enforce the decision

Key.Rationale: The Supreme Court has no authority to enforce any of its decisions. Therefore, the president and Congress could refuse to enforce a decision and thereby lessen the impact of the decision.

Content: Which of the following provides the most accurate explanation of how consumer-driven media increases partisan polarization?

A.Choice: Consumer-driven media tends to avoid discussing controversial political topics.

Key.Rationale: Consumer-driven media often focuses on controversial topics rather than avoiding them.

B.Choice: Consumer-driven media reinforces existing political biases in individuals.

Key.Rationale: Consumer-driven media increase partisan polarization because it reinforces existing biases in individuals.

C.Choice: Consumer-driven media relies heavily on corporate advertising.

Key.Rationale: Relying on corporate advertising does not explain an increase in partisan polarization.

D.Choice: Consumer-driven media is overwhelmingly conservative.

Key.Rationale: There is both liberal and conservative consumer-driven media.

Content: In The Federalist `70`, Alexander Hamilton states that “energy in the executive is a leading character in the definition of good government.” In this statement, Hamilton is arguing in favor of the need for

A.Choice: a `text(single)` executive who can respond quickly to crises

Key.Rationale: Hamilton argues in favor of a `text(single)` executive that can respond quickly to crises.

B.Choice: a president who has a good understanding of public policy

Key.Rationale: The need for a president with a good understanding of public policy is not Hamilton's central argument.

C.Choice: an electoral college in the selection of the president

Key.Rationale: Hamilton does not argue in favor of an electoral college in The Federalist `70`.

D.Choice: a president who is youthful and assertive

Key.Rationale: The quotation refers to energy in the executive, but this is not an argument for a youthful president.

Content: Which of the following Supreme Court decisions allows public school students to wear T-shirts protesting a school board decision that eliminates funding for high school arts programs?

A.Choice: Engel v. Vitale (`text(1962)`)

Key.Rationale: The Supreme Court held in Engel v. Vitale (`text(1962)`) that school sponsorship of religious activities violates the establishment clause.

B.Choice: Wisconsin v. Yoder (`text(1972)`)

Key.Rationale: The Supreme Court held in Wisconsin v. Yoder (`text(1972)`) that compelling Amish students to attend school past the `text(eighth grade)` violated the free exercise clause.

C.Choice: Tinker v. Des Moines Independent Community School District (`text(1969)`)

Key.Rationale: The Supreme Court held in Tinker v. Des Moines Independent Community School District (`text(1969)`) that students' symbolic speech is protected under the `text(First)` Amendment.

D.Choice: New York Times Co. v. United States (`text(1971)`)

Key.Rationale: The Supreme Court held in New York Times Company v. United States (`text(1971)`) that the government could not engage in prior restraint against the media.

Content: Concurrent powers have which of the following effects on the United States political system?

A.Choice: They reinforce the expansion of the power of the national government and the supremacy of the national law.

Key.Rationale: Concurrent powers do not necessarily reinforce the powers of the national government and supremacy of national law.

B.Choice: They eliminate disputes between the states and the national government by creating completely separate spheres of influence.

Key.Rationale: Concurrent powers are powers that both states and the national government have, so they do not create separate spheres of influence.

C.Choice: They foster cooperation between the states and the national government by requiring that the `text(two)` levels of government work together.

Key.Rationale: Concurrent powers do not necessarily lead to cooperation between states and the national government, and they do not require the `text(two)` levels of government to work together.

D.Choice: They make it possible for the states and the national government to simultaneously exercise influence in the same areas of public policy.

Key.Rationale: Concurrent powers are powers that both states and the national government have. They make it possible for states and the national government to simultaneously exercise influence in the same areas of public policy.

Content: Which of the following scenarios best illustrates a member of Congress supporting pork-barrel legislation?

A.Choice: A senator from a coal-producing state voting against a job-training program for coal miners

Key.Rationale: A senator from a coal-producing state voting against a job-training program for coal miners is the opposite of pork-barrel legislation.

B.Choice: A member of the House voting for urban renewal in exchange for increased funding for roads

Key.Rationale: The action described here — a member of the House voting for urban renewal in exchange for increase road funding — is not an illustration of pork-barrel legislation.

C.Choice: A senator from an agricultural state amending legislation to establish a potato research institute in his or her state

Key.Rationale: Pork-barrel legislation is characterized as the appropriation of government funds for local projects that serve a representative's constituents. Therefore, a senator from an agricultural state amending legislation to establish a potato research institute is an illustration of this concept.

D.Choice: A member of the House Armed Services Committee marking up a bill that will increase funding for military bases

Key.Rationale: A member of the House Armed Services Committee marking up a bill that will increase funding for military bases is not an example of a pork-barrel project, because the markup is for military bases in general, not a specific local constituency.

Content: If voters are acting according to the retrospective model of voting, which of the following will be the most important consideration in their decision?

A.Choice: The party affiliations of the candidates

Key.Rationale: It is common for voters to use party affiliations of the candidates when making vote choices, but this is not the most important consideration in the retrospective model of voting.

B.Choice: The campaign promises made by the candidates

Key.Rationale: Campaign promises made by candidates are prospective and therefore not part of the retrospective model of voting.

C.Choice: The effect of recent economic conditions on the voters

Key.Rationale: In the retrospective voting model, voters use recent events and conditions, such as the economy, to make their decision when voting.

D.Choice: Whether the candidates will act in the best interest of the voters if elected

Key.Rationale: Whether the candidates will act in the best interest of the voters if elected is not part of the retrospective model of voting.

Content: During his confirmation hearing, Chief Justice John Roberts stated that Roe v. Wade (`text(1973)`) “is the settled law of the land.” This statement suggests that in a case that challenges the constitutionality of legislation restricting privacy and reproductive rights, which of the following should be a key factor in the court's ruling?

A.Choice: Briefs submitted by interested parties

Key.Rationale: Briefs submitted by interested parties are called amicus curiae briefs.

B.Choice: Contemporary societal norms

Key.Rationale: Supreme Court justices are relatively shielded from societal norms and pressures when deciding cases.

C.Choice: The consensus of the other justices

Key.Rationale: While Supreme Court justices may confer with each other when hearing cases, this is not a key factor in making decisions.

D.Choice: Reliance on legal precedent

Key.Rationale: Legal precedent refers to using rulings on prior cases as the basis for current cases, which is what Chief Justice Roberts was referring to when he made a statement about Roe v. Wade.

Content: Which of the following sets of policies appears to be most influenced by a libertarian ideology?

A.Choice: Increase income taxes on the wealthy to raise revenue for social security benefits.

Key.Rationale: Libertarians do not advocate increasing income taxes on the wealthy.

B.Choice: Legalize the commercial sale of marijuana and reduce government spending on prisons.

Key.Rationale: Libertarians believe that marijuana should be legalized and sold commercially and that the government should spend less on prisons.

C.Choice: Eliminate the estate tax and promote government-funded prekindergarten education.

Key.Rationale: Libertarians believe in fewer taxes but do not believe in government promotion of education.

D.Choice: Expand the welfare state and reduce spending on national defense.

Key.Rationale: Expanding the welfare state and reducing spending on defense are tenets of liberal ideology.

Content: A state government places security cameras facing a popular site of protest in a public square in front of its statehouse. This scenario illustrates

A.Choice: how political attitudes quickly shift in the United States

Key.Rationale: The scenario does not illustrate anything about shifting political attitudes.

B.Choice: the balance of promoting stability and ensuring civil liberties

Key.Rationale: The scenario illustrates the inherent tension between civil liberties and security.

C.Choice: the free-rider problem of organizing a civil rights protest

Key.Rationale: The free-rider problem occurs when someone enjoys benefits without paying any costs, and it is not applicable in this case.

D.Choice: the impact of globalization on individual political attitudes

Key.Rationale: The impact of globalization is not best illustrated with the placement of security cameras in front of a public square.

Content: Which of the following scenarios best reflects the process of political socialization?

A.Choice: An individual takes a civics course in school and develops opinions about politics.

Key.Rationale: Important agents of political socialization include school, so an individual taking a civics course is a good example of the process of political socialization.

B.Choice: Members of Congress increasingly vote the same way as other members of their party.

Key.Rationale: Members of Congress who vote the same way as other members of their party may be the result of actions such as political pressure, but they are not demonstrating political socialization.

C.Choice: A group is able to attract new members by offering access to a broad network of people.

Key.Rationale: New members being offered access to a broad network of people is perhaps an example of socialization, but it is not an example of political socialization because there is no politics involved.

D.Choice: As media choices increase, individuals expand their media consumption to new sources.

Key.Rationale: The consumption of new sources media is not a reflection of political socialization because there are many different types of media, and lots of media are not political.

Content: Which of the following scenarios best illustrates a formal check on the power of the bureaucracy?

A.Choice: A lobbyist representing the National Rifle Association refusing to meet with employees from the Department of Homeland Security

Key.Rationale: Lobbyists from any organization are not formal checks on the power of the bureaucracy.

B.Choice: The secretary of defense being called to testify before a congressional committee

Key.Rationale: The secretary of defense is part of the bureaucracy, and calling on him or her to testify illustrates a formal check on power.

C.Choice: The White House chief of staff being formally censured by the president for publicly speaking out against the president's policy goals

Key.Rationale: The White House chief of staff is part of the executive branch and is therefore not part of the bureaucracy.

D.Choice: A federal judge being impeached for making legal decisions based on bribes

Key.Rationale: The impeachment of a federal judge is a check on the judiciary, not on the bureaucracy.

Content: In a public opinion poll, a polling company used an online survey tool to randomly contact respondents who did not have telephone lines in addition to contacting people over the phone. Which of the following best explains this decision?

A.Choice: The company saved money because it did not need to hire as many telephone interviewers to conduct the poll.

Key.Rationale: The company did not necessarily save money by using this method.

B.Choice: The company was establishing a benchmark poll at the beginning of a campaign.

Key.Rationale: This method is not exclusively associated with benchmark polling.

C.Choice: The company was interested in asking different questions to different individuals.

Key.Rationale: This method did not permit the company to ask different questions of different individuals.

D.Choice: The company wanted to ensure that the sample of the population was truly random.

Key.Rationale: This method would help ensure a random sample, since many people no longer use telephone lines for communication.

Content: Which of the following is an accurate comparison of rights protected and not protected by the `text(First)` Amendment?

A.Choice:
`ultext(Protected)` by the `text(First)` Amendment: Libel/slander
`ultext(Not Protected)` by the `text(First)` Amendment: Fighting words

Key.Rationale: Libel and slander are not protected by the `text(First)` Amendment.

B.Choice:
`ultext(Protected)` by the `text(First)` Amendment: Freedom of religion
`ultext(Not Protected)` by the `text(First)` Amendment: Freedom of assembly

Key.Rationale: Freedom of assembly is protected by the `text(First)` Amendment.

C.Choice:
`ultext(Protected)` by the `text(First)` Amendment: The right to burn a flag
`ultext(Not Protected)` by the `text(First)` Amendment: Obscenity

Key.Rationale: The right to burn a flag is protected by the `text(First)` Amendment, however obscenity, although usually legal, is not always considered protected speech.

D.Choice:
`ultext(Protected)` by the `text(First)` Amendment: Online newspapers
`ultext(Not Protected)` by the `text(First)` Amendment: The right of a student to pray in school

Key.Rationale: The right of a student to pray in school is protected by the `text(First)` Amendment.

Content: Which of the following is the correct pairing of powers found in the Articles of Confederation and powers found in the Constitution?

A.Choice:
`ultext(Articles of Confederation)`: Protection of individual liberties
`ultext(United States Constitution)`: No protection of specific individual rights

Key.Rationale: The Articles of Confederation did not contain specific protections of individual liberties. Such rights were instead enumerated in the `text(first ten)` amendments to the United States Constitution.

B.Choice:
`ultext(Articles of Confederation)`: Powerful executive branch
`ultext(United States Constitution)`: Federal government supreme over states

Key.Rationale: The Articles of Confederation did not establish a strong federal union with a powerful executive branch, though the Constitution did establish federal supremacy in Article `text(VI)`.

C.Choice:
`ultext(Articles of Confederation)`: Unicameral legislature
`ultext(United States Constitution)`: Bicameral legislature

Key.Rationale: Under the Articles of Confederation, legislation was approved by the unicameral Congress of the Confederation. The United States Constitution established a bicameral legislature consisting of the Senate and House of Representatives.

D.Choice:
`ultext(Articles of Confederation)`: Amendment requires unanimity of all states
`ultext(United States Constitution)`: Amendment requires the president's approval

Key.Rationale: Amending the United States Constitution requires ratification by `text(three-fourths)` of state legislatures or ratifying conventions but does not require presidential approval.

Content: Which of the following accurately compares the formal and informal powers of the president?

A.Choice:
`ultext(Formal Power)`: Vetoing legislation to prevent a bill from becoming law
`ultext(Informal Power)`: Using a pocket veto to prevent a bill from becoming law

Key.Rationale: Both the choice to veto and the choice to delay action on a bill to prevent it from becoming law are formal powers of the presidency under the United States Constitution.

B.Choice:
`ultext(Formal Power)`: Using the bully pulpit to influence public opinion
`ultext(Informal Power)`: Appointing ambassadors and receiving diplomats from other nations

Key.Rationale: The president's influence on public opinion is not a formal power of the presidency enumerated in the Constitution, while the appointing of ambassadors is a formal power explicitly outlined in the Constitution.

C.Choice:
`ultext(Formal Power)`: Acting as commander in chief of the military
`ultext(Informal Power)`: Signing executive agreements with foreign nations

Key.Rationale: The president's role as commander in chief of the armed forces is a formal power explicitly authorized in the Constitution. The signing of executive agreements with foreign nations is not included in the Constitution and is considered to be an informal power of the presidency.

D.Choice:
`ultext(Formal Power)`: Using the power of the purse to support government programs
`ultext(Informal Power)`: Using signing statements to shape legislation

Key.Rationale: Congress, not the president, controls the national budget.

Content: Which of the following makes a correct comparison between political parties and interest groups in the United States?

A.Choice:
`ultext(Political Parties)`: Political parties recruit and run candidates in elections.
`ultext(Interest Groups)`: Interest groups seek to influence public policy.

Key.Rationale: Political parties primarily focus on running candidates for office, while interest groups seek to influence public policy.

B.Choice:
`ultext(Political Parties)`: Political parties have small constituencies and thus try to win elections by energizing their base to vote for them.
`ultext(Interest Groups)`: Interest groups alert and educate voters regarding pending legislation.

Key.Rationale: Constituency size varies based on the geographical scope of the political office in question, but political parties frequently control large portions of a given constituency.

C.Choice:
`ultext(Political Parties)`: Political parties have organizations that donate money to candidates for public office.
`ultext(Interest Groups)`: Interest groups are barred by law from donating money to political campaigns.

Key.Rationale: Political parties can do fund-raising for their candidates within the party organization, but they do not typically control external organizations. Interest groups are not barred from seeking to influence policy by donating to campaigns.

D.Choice:
`ultext(Political Parties)`: Political parties achieve the bulk of the changes they seek through the use of the courts.
`ultext(Interest Groups)`: Interest groups build relationships with congressional committees and the bureaucracy to form iron triangles.

Key.Rationale: Political parties usually seek to make policy through legislation.

Content: Which of the following sets of Supreme Court cases best illustrates how views of federalism have shifted in the United States?

A.Choice:
`ultext(Case 1)`: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka (`text(1954)`) 
`ultext(Case 2)`: Baker v. Carr (`text(1962)`)

Key.Rationale: Neither Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka nor Baker v. Carr dealt explicitly with issues of federalism.

B.Choice:
`ultext(Case 1)`: McCulloch v. Maryland (`text(1819)`) 
`ultext(Case 2)`: United States v. Lopez (`text(1995)`)

Key.Rationale: McCulloch v. Maryland established that states did not have the power to tax federal institutions, such as the Bank of the United States. United States v. Lopez demonstrated a shift in federal authority by ruling that the federal government could not establish gun- free zones under the commerce clause.

C.Choice:
`ultext(Case 1)`: Roe v. Wade (`text(1973)`)
`ultext(Case 2)`: McDonald v. Chicago (`text(2010)`)

Key.Rationale: Neither Roe v. Wade nor McDonald v. Chicago dealt explicitly with issues of federalism.

D.Choice:
`ultext(Case 1)`: Schenck v. United States (`text(1919)`) 
`ultext(Case 2)`: New York Times v. United States (`text(1971)`)

Key.Rationale: Neither Schenck v. United States nor New York Times v. United States dealt explicitly with issues of federalism.

Content: Which of the following describes the potential impact on the electorate when `text(daily)` media coverage of elections focuses primarily on the newest poll results?

A.Choice: The electorate will be increasingly divided along partisan lines.

Key.Rationale: Media coverage of poll results does not necessarily have an impact on the level of partisanship among voters.

B.Choice: The electorate will be less likely to turn out to vote on Election Day.

Key.Rationale: Media coverage of poll results does not necessarily have a negative impact on voter turnout.

C.Choice: The electorate will be more likely to have expanded knowledge of the electoral process.

Key.Rationale: Media coverage of poll results does not improve public understanding of the electoral process.

D.Choice: The electorate will be less able to accurately compare the policy platforms of candidates running in the election.

Key.Rationale: Media coverage that focuses primarily on poll results devotes less time and resources to educating the electorate on matters of policy.

Content: Which of the following is an example of how separation of powers creates friction between the executive and legislative branches in the policy-making process?

A.Choice: The electoral college vote ends with no candidate receiving a majority of the votes, and the House of Representatives is delegated the task of selecting the next president.

Key.Rationale: The breaking of an electoral college tie by the House of Representatives is not an example of friction with the executive branch.

B.Choice: The Senate votes to impeach a sitting president for high crimes and misdemeanors.

Key.Rationale: Impeachment proceedings in the Senate for offenses committed by the executive demonstrate effective checks and balances, not friction over separated powers.

C.Choice: The secretary of state is dispatched along with a delegation of senators to negotiate a treaty with a foreign government.

Key.Rationale: The dispatch of the secretary of state along with the Senate delegation is within the power of the executive to negotiate treaties and conduct foreign affairs.

D.Choice: The president threatens to issue an executive order for stricter gun control if Congress continues to refuse to take action.

Key.Rationale: The president's threat to legislate by executive order creates friction with the legislative branch, since passing laws is within the legislature's purview.

Content: Which of the following scenarios is an example of the trustee model of representation?

A.Choice: The NAACP leadership sends representatives to Washington to lobby for changes to the Voting Rights Act.

Key.Rationale: The dispatch of representatives to lobby for a particular reform on behalf of an interest group does not fall under a specific model of representation.

B.Choice: Congress passes a bill allocating money to clean up nuclear waste sites after a wave of large-scale peaceful protests.

Key.Rationale: The passage of legislation to address a cause brought to the attention of Congress by a wave of popular protest more closely reflects a delegate model of representation.

C.Choice: A member of Congress votes to close a popular tax loophole based on the belief that the money would be better spent paying down the national debt.

Key.Rationale: The trustee model of representation involves elected officials voting in whatever manner they feel best serves their constituents, regardless of popular opinion regarding the issue.

D.Choice: A presidential candidate advocates using an executive order to increase the minimum wage for federal contractors.

Key.Rationale: The proposals of a presidential candidate do not have an impact on policy and do not serve as a particular model of representation until the candidate is duly elected as a representative of the people.

Content: `text(Two)` interest groups are competing for influence in Congress. `text(One)` group represents banking institutions, while the other advocates for consumer protections. A critic of the influence of interest groups would make which of the following claims?

A.Choice: The interest groups will nominate a slate of candidates for office to compete against each other in the next election in order to determine which interests prevail.

Key.Rationale: Interest groups do not nominate slates of candidates; this is the function of political parties.

B.Choice: The consumer protection group will appeal only to Republican leaders, while the banking interests will appeal only to Democratic leaders.

Key.Rationale: The protection of banking interests is more likely to appeal to Republicans, while the consumer protection group is more likely to appeal to Democrats.

C.Choice: The banking interest group likely has greater financial resources and access to policy makers than the consumer protection group.

Key.Rationale: The institution representing banking interests most likely has resources that outweigh those of a group seeking to protect consumers.

D.Choice: The consumer protection group is prohibited by federal regulations from direct lobbying.

Key.Rationale: Neither interest group is prohibited by federal regulations from direct lobbying.

Content: In which of the following situations would the Supreme Court be most likely to utilize the doctrine of selective incorporation?

A.Choice: When an individual claims that a right protected by the Bill of Rights is infringed upon by a state

Key.Rationale: Selective incorporation ensures that states and localities cannot pass laws that infringe upon the rights guaranteed in the United States Constitution.

B.Choice: When there is a conflict among the branches of the national government

Key.Rationale: Conflict between the different branches of the federal government is not affected by selective incorporation, which ensures that states localities cannot pass laws that infringe upon the rights guaranteed in the United States Constitution.

C.Choice: When a federal policy shifting oversight authority from a national agency to a state agency is challenged

Key.Rationale: Conflict over state versus federal authority for oversight is not affected by selective incorporation, which ensures that states and localities cannot pass laws that infringe upon the rights guaranteed in the United States Constitution.

D.Choice: When a former employee files a wrongful termination claim against a company headquartered in another state

Key.Rationale: Wrongful termination suits that cross state lines are not affected by selective incorporation, which ensures that states and localities cannot pass laws that infringe upon the rights guaranteed in the United States Constitution.

Content: Which of the following is a true statement about the role of the media in providing citizens with information?

A.Choice: Investigative reporting dominates the news because it is less expensive than political commentary.

Key.Rationale: Investigative reporting tends to compose a smaller part of the news because it typically requires more resources than political commentary.

B.Choice: Demand for instantaneous news reporting has led to the growth of `text(24-hour)` news operations and a shift to online media consumption.

Key.Rationale: The increased popularity of `text(24-hour)` news networks and online media emerged from public demand for instant coverage of news events.

C.Choice: The media is increasingly controlled by the major political parties, who determine which stories are covered by the press.

Key.Rationale: Media in the United States, though influenced by interest groups, is not in the control of major political parties.

D.Choice: There has been an increase in social media and Internet news consumption by the public, causing the top `text(five)` media conglomerates to have greater control over public opinion.

Key.Rationale: The increased consumption of news content from the Internet and the influence of social media have created a greater number of outlets for public opinion rather than consolidating control in the hands of media conglomerates.

Content: A public school district implemented a policy that allowed students to vote on whether they wanted a student-led prayer to be read at football games. This policy was later found to be unconstitutional by the United States Supreme Court. Which of the following clauses did the policy most likely violate?

A.Choice: The interstate commerce clause

Key.Rationale: The interstate commerce clause allows the federal government to regulate commerce between the states, and the establishment of prayer at a football game would not violate this constitutional principle.

B.Choice: The free exercise clause

Key.Rationale: The free exercise clause guarantees individuals the freedom to practice their religion, but it does not prohibit the establishment of laws or policies based on religion.

C.Choice: The supremacy clause

Key.Rationale: The supremacy clause establishes the primacy of the federal Constitution over state laws, which has no bearing on the establishment of prayer at a football game.

D.Choice: The establishment clause

Key.Rationale: The establishment clause prohibits the government from creating any law or policy that favors a specific religion or institutionalizes its religious practice and belief.

Content: Which of the following policies would an individual who identifies as a Democrat most likely support?

A.Choice: Reducing regulations on Wall Street to stimulate economic growth

Key.Rationale: Democrats do not support reducing regulations on Wall Street.

B.Choice: Decreasing the role of the federal government to ensure access to health care

Key.Rationale: Democrats support increasing the role of the federal government to ensure access to health care.

C.Choice: Increasing federal enforcement of immigration laws

Key.Rationale: Democrats do not support increasing the enforcement of immigration laws.

D.Choice: Strengthening anti-discrimination policies for married gay couples

Key.Rationale: Democrats support antidiscrimination policies for gay couples getting married.

Content: The following is from the `text(2016)` Republican Party Platform.

:ibox:“Because the Federal Reserve's monetary policy decisions affect job creation, upward mobility for workers, and equitable prosperity, they should be transparent. Similarly, the Federal Reserve's important role as a lender of last resort should also be carried out in a more transparent manner. The Republican Party will advance legislation that brings transparency and accountability to the Federal Reserve, the Federal Open Market Committee, and the Federal Reserve's dealing with foreign banks.”

	https://www.gop.com/the-2016-republican-party-platform/
After reading the scenario, respond to A, B, and C below.
Describe an action, other than advancing legislation, that members of Congress may take to bring transparency and accountability to the Federal Reserve.

In the context of this section of the Republican Party platform, explain how the proposal to increase transparency and accountability described in part A would affect the Federal Reserve's ability to make economic policy.
Explain how ideological differences between the parties might affect Democratic Party support of the proposal.

In `text(2010)` Arizona passed a law that sought to reduce the number of undocumented immigrants in the state. The law made it a crime to seek or obtain work in the state without proper documentation, and it also made hiring, sheltering, or transporting undocumented people illegal. It also gave local law enforcement the authority to require proof of residency in the course of a lawful arrest, and it gave them the authority to perform warrantless stops of people they suspected of being undocumented.

The United States Department of Justice challenged the state law as an interference with the national government's enumerated powers to regulate and enforce immigration law. In Arizona v. United States (`text(2012)`), the Supreme Court agreed with the United States in a `6-3` decision stating most of the provisions of the law did conflict with federal authority. The Court said, “The Government of the United States has broad, undoubted power over the subject of immigration and the status of aliens... This authority rests, in part, on the National Government's constitutional power to establish an uniform Rule of Naturalization, and its inherent power as sovereign to control and conduct relations with foreign nations.”
Based on the information above, respond to the following questions.
Identify a common constitutional principle used to make a ruling in both McCulloch v. Maryland (`text(1819)`) and Arizona v. United States (`text(2012)`).
Explain how the facts of McCulloch v. Maryland and the facts of Arizona v. United States led to a similar holding in both cases.
Describe an action that Congress could take to respond to the Arizona v. United States decision if it disagreed with the decision.

Equality of opportunity is a central value in the American political system. Choose either Congress or the Supreme Court, and present an argument for why your choice is most responsible for advancing the principle of equality of opportunity in the United States.
In your essay, you must:

:ibox:• Articulate a defensible claim or thesis that responds to the prompt and establishes a line of reasoning.

• Support your claim with at least `text(TWO)` pieces of accurate and relevant information.

• At least `text(ONE)` piece of evidence must be from the list below.

`1`) Constitutional amendments
`2`) The Declaration of Independence
`3`) Federalist `78`

• The `text(second)` piece of evidence must be from a different source on the list above OR from your knowledge of Congress or the Supreme Court.

• Use reasoning to explain why your evidence supports your claim/thesis.
